title: 394 - Mega Man 3
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Mega Man 3
items.description: The episode's game: Capcom's 1990 NES sequel that adds the slide, Rush the robot dog and the Doc Robot stages.

links.label: Mega Man 3 (NES) - The Cutting Room Floor

items.name: Mega Man
items.description: The first game in the series, voted onto the Essential Games List; the hosts debate whether it still belongs.

items.name: Mega Man 2
items.description: The previous NES game, also on the Essential Games List, whose bosses return as Doc Robot in this game.

items.name: Mega Man (franchise)
items.description: The Capcom action-platformer series; this is its third NES entry, with Mega Man 11 the latest numbered game mentioned.

items.name: Capcom
items.description: The developer and publisher behind Mega Man, putting out a game nearly every year.

items.name: Mega Man X
items.description: Super Nintendo entry in the spinoff series that one host owned as a kid and loved.

items.name: Mega Man 8
items.description: A later PlayStation-era entry in the series that one host remembers playing.

items.name: Mega Man Anniversary Collection
items.description: The PS2 and GameCube compilation of Mega Man 1 to 8, with a Navi Mode, that one host found too hard.

items.name: Yellow Devil
items.description: The giant block-throwing Wily boss, back as Yellow Devil Mark 2; a wall for one host.

items.name: Keiji Inafune
items.description: Mega Man artist who said Mega Man 3 is one of his least favorite entries.

links.label: Wikipedia: Keiji Inafune
links.note: Japanese video game producer, illustrator, and businessman (born 1965)

links.label: How Mega Man survived its creator leaving Capcom - Kotaku

items.name: Akira Kitamura
items.description: Lead of the first two games, who left Capcom early in this game's development.

items.name: Mega Man 3 second-controller debug features
items.description: Leftover debug features in the NES game: super jump, slowed and frozen animations when using controller two.

links.label: Mega Man 3 Tips and Tricks - StrategyWiki

items.name: Rockman Complete Works
items.description: The Japan-only PlayStation remake of Rockman 3, with a Navi Mode that adds hint pop-ups.

items.name: Mega Man: The Wily Wars
items.description: The Sega Genesis remake of Mega Man 1 to 3 with 16-bit graphics and changed physics.

links.label: Wikipedia: Mega Man: The Wily Wars
Mega Man: The Wily Wars - Giant Bomb

items.name: Mega Man Soccer
items.description: A Super Nintendo spin-off soccer game the hosts could hardly believe exists.

links.label: Wikipedia: Mega Man Soccer
links.note: 1994 sports video game published by Capcom

items.name: Mega Man 4
items.description: The next NES game, whose big change one host knows but will not spoil.

items.name: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
items.description: Contest winner Chris Houlihan got his name in a secret house in this game.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past

items.name: Kingdom Hearts
items.description: Its secret boss Kurt Zisa was named after a fan who won a name-in-game contest.

items.name: Pokemon Gold and Silver
items.description: Compared to Mega Man 3's return to earlier bosses, like going back to Kanto.

items.name: Castlevania
items.description: Mentioned for credits that list made-up names, and for its knockback.

items.name: Super Smash Bros.
items.description: Nintendo crossover fighter where Mega Man, Samus and Simon appear; the hosts mention its DLC and long roster.

items.name: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3
items.description: Its revert is the example for a single mechanic that changes a sequel.

items.name: Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster
items.description: Remaster with adjustable settings, such as boosted experience, used as a model for a Mega Man 3 remaster.

links.label: Wikipedia: Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster
links.note: Series of Final Fantasy video game remasters

items.name: Journey
items.description: Brought up in a joke about not knowing you play online; the game is a wordless adventure.

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: The show's list of NES games that define the system; Mega Man 3 is voted on at the end.
